component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the engagement against a finalized work plan that details every task, resource and schedule element and explicitly recognizes MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans. The component delivers the kick-off meeting to review scope, schedule and communications protocol, quarterly status meetings with written minutes, monthly email and phone progress updates, and quarterly written updates timed to the last working day of March, June, September and December so they feed the SPR Quarterly Report. It also carries the duty to consult MHTC's representative on administration concerns and to coordinate fully with, and keep advice available to, the Construction and Materials Division throughout the agreement. The whole schedule is planned inside the RFP's 15-month contract period, with all meetings, presentations and calls held between 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. Central.

component_records.title: Data Management Plan and research data handling
component_records.description: Within two weeks of kick-off the team submits a Data Management Plan describing the anticipated formats of all data and related files, and committing to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats so the corpus and outputs stay usable after the contract ends. The DMP is treated as a living document, updated as the property corpus and model artifacts take shape, and it governs how MHTC-supplied plans, deeds and survey information are stored and who may access them. It is delivered as a task deliverable alongside meeting agendas and minutes.

component_records.title: Literature search and state-of-practice review
component_records.description: A structured review of published research and other state DOTs' use of AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, covering peer-reviewed literature, DOT research reports and documented agency pilots. The review is scoped to ROW use cases relevant to legal land descriptions, records the search strategy and inclusion criteria so the method is auditable, and produces an annotated findings memo that feeds the synthesis report and the design of the drafting tool. It is completed early so its lessons shape the proof of concept rather than trailing it.

component_records.title: MHTC parameter and EPG 236.4.6.2 drafting rulebook
component_records.description: Before any model work, the team works with MoDOT ROW staff to codify the MHTC parameters and the EPG Section 236.4.6.2 requirements into an explicit, testable drafting rulebook. The rulebook encodes the metes-and-bounds convention for rights acquired or conveyed, the rule that a whole-property acquisition is described exactly as it appears on the last deed of record, the recital of specific rights where less than fee simple is taken, and the lot-call and 1/4-1/4 call forms. It becomes the acceptance standard against which every generated draft is checked, and it is the artifact that lets the study answer whether AI/ML is genuinely useful for producing a first draft under MHTC parameters.

component_records.title: LLD development program nomination and IS approval
component_records.description: The team names the specific program used to develop the LLDs and submits it to MoDOT Information Systems for approval before any proof-of-concept work proceeds, with a documented package covering version, hosting model, licensing position, data handling and security posture. The nomination is deliberately made against the approved-technology baseline: .NET 6.0 or above with MVC/Razor Pages/Web API, C#/JavaScript/CSS/HTML, Python only for ESRI scripts or small one-time uses, and no third-party component that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without BRPT and IS management review. Approval is treated as a gated milestone, so no Task 3c effort is committed until it is granted.

component_records.title: Proof-of-concept drafting tool and demonstration
component_records.description: A web-based drafting application, requiring only a modern browser, that ingests right-of-way plans, deeds and survey information and generates a first-draft legal land description for MoDOT review and feedback. It is built on MVC/Razor Pages/Web API with C# and JavaScript, meets WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri accessibility standard, carries no vendor branding where a licensed option removes it, and uses only properly licensed third-party content. The demonstration walks MoDOT through drafts for a variety of property types, including whole-property acquisitions described from the last deed of record, and captures reviewer feedback as a measured improvement loop that answers the usefulness question.

component_records.title: Data platform, PII controls and security compliance
component_records.description: The tool's persistence layer is deployed on Oracle 19C on premise, with any SQL Server alternative pursued only through the MoDOT IS Data Service Management approval route, and the design keeps PII out of the database entirely by working from parcel and deed records rather than personal data. Where a specific business need for PII is later identified, storage is gated on IS Cyber Security Team approval before any table is created. Confidential factual matters supplied by MHTC are held under a defined handling convention, disclosed to no third party except as statute, ordinance, court order or MHTC's representative authorizes, and any request for such information is escalated to MHTC at once.

component_records.title: ROW staff training and user manual
component_records.description: Once the tool is finalized, the team delivers hands-on training to MoDOT ROW staff and a user manual written for staff reference, covering the drafting workflow, how to review and correct a generated first draft, the EPG 236.4.6.2 checks the draft must pass, and the surveyor review step that precedes deed presentation. Training is delivered in a train-the-trainer format with recorded sessions so MoDOT can onboard later staff without further cost, and the manual is delivered electronically in a non-proprietary format consistent with the Data Management Plan. Both are updated to reflect the final tool before the draft final report is submitted.

component_records.title: Interim presentation and reporting milestones
component_records.description: An interim presentation near the project mid-point updates MoDOT on progress, early findings and project direction, and is used to confirm the remaining scope before finalization. It is scheduled against the milestone table and delivered in person or online to suit MoDOT, with the slide deck and a written progress summary issued as records of the event. This component also holds the schedule logic that ties the demonstration, training, interim presentation and draft final report to their fixed dates.

component_records.title: Synthesis report, final report and research summary
component_records.description: A draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary are delivered as complete products, final except for revisions arising from MoDOT's review, together with the supporting documentation the study identifies as beneficial. The final report then documents every task completed and all findings, follows the Publication Guidelines and summary template, and includes a completed Technical Report Documentation page. A separate 1-2 page research summary states the objectives, findings and conclusions, and a presentation for MoDOT staff covers the significant results. All materials are delivered to MHTC as its property, with no public release without MHTC's representative's prior consent.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and insurance obligations
component_records.description: A compliance workstream accepts the RFP's contract provisions and the post-award negotiated contract, including MHTC's right to cancel the award if terms cannot be agreed, and holds that written clarifications from MHTC govern over conflicting proposal text. It covers the employment-eligibility obligations: Executive Order 07-13 compliance, the signed certification that assigned employees are authorized to work, the E-Verify MOU, the sworn affidavit of non-employment of unauthorized aliens, and lawful-presence proof for sole proprietors and general partners. It also carries the flow-down of Section (3) paragraph I into every subcontract, MHTC-directed enforcement action, the no-assignment rule, records retention and Auditor access for three years after final payment, and certificates of General Liability, Automobile Liability and Missouri Workmen's Compensation at the stated limits. The Offeror remains solely liable to MHTC for quality and performance regardless of subcontractors, and pursues the 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation goals and direct hiring of minorities and women.
